sec: Adrenal medulla: development, catecholamines and biosynthesis · p852

items.q: Match adrenal embryology — 1) Adrenal medulla  2) Adrenal cortex … A) Mesoderm (80%)  B) Neuroectoderm (20%)
items.exp: Medulla (20%) is neuroectodermal; cortex (80%) mesodermal; development completed by the 45th day of IUL. (Book p852)

items.q: Adrenal development is completed by the ___ day of intra-uterine life.
items.exp: Development is completed on the 45th day of IUL. (Book p852)

items.q: By the 80/20 rule, adrenaline (epinephrine) forms what share of medullary catecholamines?
items.exp: Adrenaline/epinephrine 80% (smaller granules), noradrenaline/norepinephrine 20% (larger dense granules); secretion is pulsatile. (Book p852)

items.q: Match catecholamine to metabolite — 1) Adrenaline  2) Dopamine  3) Noradrenaline … A) Homovanillic acid (HVA)  B) Normetanephrine  C) Metanephrine and VMA
items.exp: Adrenaline → metanephrine/VMA; dopamine → HVA; noradrenaline → normetanephrine (metabolites are easier to measure). (Book p852)

items.q: The rate-limiting step of catecholamine biosynthesis (tyrosine → DOPA) is catalysed by ___.
items.exp: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting step; the ladder is tyrosine → DOPA → dopamine → NE → epinephrine. (Book p852)

items.q: The enzyme converting norepinephrine to epinephrine is:
items.exp: PNMT (phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase) converts NE to epinephrine. (Book p852)

items.q: ‘PNMT is present only in the adrenal gland, so extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas produce only norepinephrine.’
opts: False — extra-adrenal tumours make only epinephrine
items.exp: PNMT is adrenal-only; extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma lacks it and produces only NE. (Book p852)

items.q: The metabolic relation between cortex and medulla is:
items.exp: Cortisol from the cortex stimulates medullary PNMT. (Book p852)
